In 2004, 4,641 pedestrians were killed in traffic crashes in the United States — a decrease of 15 percent from the 5,489 pedestrians killed in 1994. On average, a pedestrian is killed in a traffic crash every 113 minutes and injured in a traffic crash every 8 minutes. There were 68,000 pedestrians injured in traffic crashes in 2004. Most pedestrian fatalities in 2004 occurred in urban areas (72%), at non-intersection locations (79%), in normal weather conditions (89%), and at night (66%). In 2004, nearly one-fifth (19%) of all children between the ages of 5 and 9 who were killed in traffic crashes were pedestrians.
